name: Ochanomizu University
overview:
Additional Programme Specifics

  • Only female students can apply


Ochanomizu University

Established as the Tokyo Women’s Normal School, Japan’s first national institution of higher education for women in 1875, the university will celebrate its 150th anniversary in 2025. Women aspiring to scholarship gathered here from all over the country. Ochanomizy University has blazed a path as a pioneer in women’s education, even when it was difficult for Japanese women to receive a higher education and play an active role in society. Their role has been to educate women who recognize and respect people from diverse backgrounds in gender, age, race, nationality, culture, religion, and social class among others, and help them create a better society. As its name implies, the Tokyo Women’s Normal School was established as an institution for educating future teachers. However, its graduates went on to pursue successful careers not only as educators but also as excellent researchers and leaders in fields including economics, industry, and the media
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Photocopy of Passport (ID page)
  • Academic transcript
  • A photo with no background for the Application for Certificate of Eligibility
  • Recommendation Letter (Form 1)


To be given to the campus administration:

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


Important: Applicants should be female or women-identified students only.

For those whose gender identity differs from the record on their family register or passport, Ochanomizu University can provide in advance information and guidance, such as regarding the use of rooms, to help the student after the semester begins.


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Receipt of the letter of acceptance from OIT

The result of selection will be sent to the partner university around two months after each application deadline.

The university will send you the official letter of acceptance.


3. Visa application & COE

Students who stay more than 90 days require a visa. In order to apply for a student visa, a COE (Certificate of Eligibility) is needed which will be issued by Immigration bureau in Japan. Usually, the process will take about 2 months before the original COE reaches you. Please be patient until receiving the COE.

The last step is to obtain your visa.

Upon your arrival:

  • During your immigration check after the first landing in Japan, show QR codes on the Visit Japan Web screen to an officer and answer questions.
  • Your COE will be exchanged with a “Residence Card” upon your entry into Japan.


4. Insurance and Health

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

Exchange students who will stay in Japan more than 3 months must join the National Health Insurance (NHI) regardless of the kind of insurance they may already have. This is a strict legal requirement in Japan. Once you arrive in Japan, you must complete the required procedures at your local city/ward office.


For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/japon

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


5. Campus life

  • Facilities

The campus has different facilities. You will have access to the library, the auditorium, the cafeteria, language study commons, learning commons, and an international student plaza.


  • Activities

Ochanomizu University offers a wide range of activities. There are 49 official clubs (33 cultural activities and 16 sports clubs) in total.


  • International

There are more than 200 international students from 28 countries and regions.


The university offers different supports for international students:

Tutor systems: Graduate students will support new international students with their writing and speaking skills when they need to present an assignment for the classes.

Buddy system: International students will have a "buddy" assigned by their supervisors to help them in their daily life and academic matters.

Cultural events: The Center for International Education holds cultural events every semester which are free for the international students.

Volunteer activities: The affiliated schools have activities that allow international students to become teacher assistants to teach English.
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)


Ochanomizu University has three dormitories. The Otowakan, which was newly established on campus in April 2022, is for both Japanese and international students, the Koishikawa Dormitory is for graduate students, and Ochanomizu University SCC is for first- and second-year undergraduates.

A dormitory on campus is available. All the rooms are single rooms furnished with a single bed, a shower room, a toilet, a desk, a fridge, an air conditioner, etc. Laundry machines are mutual facilities. Meals are not served.

Entrance fee: 31,680 yen (180€)

Monthly cost : 62,900 yen (355€)

(Including room rent fee, residents’ association fee, internet fee, insurance fee, and utilities except for gas.)

Joint surety fee: 4,000 yen (22€)

Model room: https://mast-net.theta360.biz/t/c60122de-1151-11ec-af35-06d61ac6b8d1-1


Off-campus accommodation


  • Shared house

One of the most popular housing options among the students is a “shared house”. A “shared house” is a property where the kitchen, living room, bathroom, etc. are shared with other residents.

Companies include: Frontier Co, Ltd balance plan, Borderless House, etc.

  • Apartments

If you want complete privacy, you can also sign up for an apartment on your own through a real estate agency. However, the cost will be a bit higher, and you may need to furnish the room yourself in some cases.

  • Homestay

If you want to experience the Japanese life style, a homestay may be an option for you.
courses:
Credits

Students must take a total of 28 local credits, i.e., 14 credits per semester to obtain 60 ECTS for the year, not counting EIP credits.

Academic Calendar

First (Spring semester): April 2026 - September 2026

Second (Fall semester): October 2026 - March 2027

Department and Courses

You will be enrolled in the Faculty of Computer Science and Information Technology and will have access to the master courses.

  • Data engineering (2 credits)

  • Data engineering seminar (2 credits)

  • Software engineering for global leader (2 credits)

  • Japanese language course (2 credits)

  • Cultural Japanese I (2 credits)

  • Cultural Japanese II (2 credits)

  • Comprehensive Japanese I (2 credits)

  • Advanced communication training (2 credits)

  • Advanced Topics on unconventional computing (2 credits)

  • Research (8 credits)

*The following classes are not fully taught in English. They’re taught in Japanese with English support.

For more details regarding the classes content: here.

Important notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).

  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.

  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.

  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.

  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial overview (4th yeat at Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees at the partner university.
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.)


Other expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: from 800€
  • Visa: 18€
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ depending on the coverage (same as above)
  • Potential deposit for your accommodation


Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the Japanese yen. 1 € = 176¥ (rate in October 2025).


Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


When coming to Japan, you should estimate that you will be spending every month between 1000€ to 1500€.


  • Housing & utilities

250 to 500€ + 40€ of utilities. The price of an apartment in the city center is approximately the same as a mid-size city in France. Rent depends on where exactly in Tokyo you choose to live.


  • Food & eating out** ~150-200€

Around 6 euros for a meal in a basic restaurant. Around 15 euros for a meal in a mid-range restaurant

The price of basic food is about the same as in France (Paris), except for imported products which will be more expensive and local products which will be cheaper.


  • Transportation ~100€


  • Health insurance ~12€


  • Phone, internet ~20-50€

We recommend you to make a mobile contract at one of discount mobile phone companies in Japan, for example: "Rakuten Mobile", "UQ mobile" provided by KDDI, "Y!mobile" by SoftBank, and Sakura Mobile. With a new SIM card, you can use your own smart phone in Japan. A previous student has recommended Rakuten for the phone plan because it is the cheapest for a good amount of data.


  • Leisure ~80-150€

The prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

Students can find the government-approved information site for studying in Japan operated by the Japan Student Services Organization through the link here.



**Food

The price of food will vary depending on whether you wish to cook for yourself or not.

Japan has a great system of readymade meals prepared at supermarkets and convenience stores that are very cheap.

You can therefore pay around 8€ a day for eating your lunch and your dinner from there.

You can sometimes pay even less as some supermarkets put discounts on meals after a certain hour.

It is entirely possible to eat a lunch and dessert for 4€ in Japan by waiting for those discounts.

It is popularly said that those meals go bad after one day and you must eat them the day they are made.

If you have a fridge, you can store them for up to two weeks.

It is therefore possible to eat for 40€ a week in Japan.

Vegetables, fruits, and rice is very expensive in Japan.

A kilo of rice itself costs between 4€ and 5€.

Anything meat related is mostly cheap.

It would overall cost as much as to eat readymade meals or cooking for yourself depending on how you eat.

Expect to therefore pay between 200€ and 300€ a month for food.
